Research preview · paper under review

Don’t update the solver.
Teach the harness to improve.

HarnessTTT trains the outer-loop proposer to write complete executable harnesses—prompt, skills, tools, and middleware—while the inner-loop executor stays frozen. The learned harness then moves to a stronger executor without retraining.

View the results Code

One score per rollout trains only the proposer’s LoRA adapter. No gradient ever reaches the executor.

Results

A frozen 9B executor, pushed by a learned harness.

With a frozen Qwen3.5-9B executor, HarnessTTT leads the compared open-weight systems of up to 10B parameters on nine of eleven tasks and improves on Finch-9B on all eleven.

The idea

Move test-time learning one level outward.

Test-time RL writes the reward into the executor’s weights. Frozen-executor systems keep a better artifact but leave their proposal policy fixed. HarnessTTT trains that policy.

01

Propose an executable harness

The proposer edits a complete harness: system prompt, skills, generated tool code, middleware, and control parameters. Every generated tool passes static checks and a sandboxed self-test before it runs.

02

Score it with a frozen executor

Each harness gets one rollout of the frozen executor under a fixed evaluator budget. Its reward is the gain over the incumbent, normalized by the remaining gap to a reference score.

03

Update only the proposer

A leave-one-out baseline with max-sharpening turns the K scores of a group into advantages for a LoRA update of the proposer. The best program and harness carry over to the next round.

Weak-to-strong transfer

A harness learned on a small model lifts a stronger one.

The learned harness is explicit and separate from the executor’s weights. We take the harnesses learned with Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.8-27B, switch the executor to GPT-5.5, and continue the search.

Bold: state of the art per task; underline: second best. For each HarnessTTT size, the first column searches with its own frozen executor and the second moves the learned harness to GPT-5.5 and continues the search. HarnessTTT matches or exceeds the frontier on eight of thirteen tasks, is within 1% on four more (Erdős, AC1, CP26, scRNA), and is behind on EPLB. LLM-SQL and Txn are quarantined in the paper, which leaves six. Because the executor changes and the search continues, these gains do not isolate a pure transfer effect.

Ablations

Where the reward goes, how wide to search, how to score.

Routing the rollout reward to the proposer’s weights reaches the highest endpoint, and reaches it sooner, than routing it to the proposer’s context or to the executor’s weights.

The 27B campaign samples 8 harnesses per round instead of 32 and uses 5 evaluator calls per rollout instead of 20; it also uses revised Hadamard, LLM-SQL, and AHC evaluators, so those columns mix model scale with evaluator changes.

            READING THE NUMBERS
            
    What these results do and do not show.
    
            
    The paper reports the selected outcome of each search campaign and states where a comparison is not clean.
    
            
      
              
    • Single campaigns. Tables report one selected run per task, not a mean over independent searches.
      • 
              
    • Quarantined tasks. LLM-SQL and Txn are excluded from the paper’s frontier claims.
      • 
              
    • Transfer is not isolated. Switching to GPT-5.5 changes the executor and adds search.
      • 
              
    • Controls describe the protocol. The released artifact does not yet include the trusted runtime needed to verify the validation gates independently.
